dzhng-skills-authoring-audit-agents.description: Audit or rewrite AGENTS.md so it holds only lasting principles. Run it only when the user asks for it by name; never invoke it on your own.

dzhng-skills-review-audit-decisions.description: Audit the decisions an implementing agent made, not its diff — a pure audit that traces the session's history into a decisions ledger, changes no code, and never blocks an unsupervised run. Working code still embeds architecture the user never chose; surface it because future work inherits it. Use when the user wants to review the decisions the AI made on their behalf, before merging or committing AI-implemented work, when integrating a delegated subagent's pass, or when a fix "works" but might be a point fix.

dzhng-skills-review-audit-performance.description: Audit and prioritize performance work through bounded-work and forward-progress checks. Use when asked to find performance issues, investigate freezes/500s/OOMs, review retries or polling for no-progress loops, rank a performance backlog, or implement the next simple performance fixes.

dzhng-skills-review-audit-tests.description: Audit whether tests earn their maintenance cost and which suite owns each contract. Use when pruning redundant tests, investigating implementation coupling or test-only production hooks, reviewing the value of proposed coverage, or auditing an entire subsystem. Use write-tests to implement the resulting test changes.

dzhng-skills-plan-auto-research.description: Run fast, progressive experiments to map tunable parameters and their effects. Use when optimizing code, prompts, configurations, or other artifacts against a goal or benchmark, or when a long research run needs a planned hypothesis queue, focused trials, and durable findings.

dzhng-skills-graphics-cinematic-shot.description: Shoot software UI like a film. A sequence of hero shots, each a steep, oblique, extreme close-up of the interface floating in black, with a razor-thin focal plane, a slow motivated camera drift, and UI that acts on its own, hard-cut on the action, ending on one line of copy and a still logo. Use when asked for a launch video, product film, feature trailer, teaser, promo clip, hero shot, or any "cinematic" footage of an app or UI. This skill covers camera, framing, light, and edit. It is stack-agnostic.

dzhng-skills-implement-claude.description: Use Claude Code as an independent `claude -p` subagent when the user explicitly asks for Claude, wants a second-agent opinion from Claude, or asks to delegate a well-scoped task to Claude. Supports selecting `--model` and thinking/effort level with defaults of the current `opus` alias and `high`.

dzhng-skills-implement-close-spec.description: When a spec under specs/<feature>/ is done shipping (a write-spec build, or any planned task that produced a spec), archive it to specs/done/ and rewrite it from a build-plan into a durable rationale — the why, the principles, the invariants — pointing back to the real code for the how. Use when implementation has landed and the plan no longer matches what shipped, or the user says a feature/spec is finished. Pairs with [write-spec](../../plan/write-spec/SKILL.md) (the plan this closes) and [review](../../review/review/SKILL.md) (run before closing).

dzhng-skills-review-code-review.description: Review changed code for naming, stale references, unnecessary complexity, and comment quality. Use after completing implementation work, before committing, or when the user asks to review or audit code.

dzhng-skills-implement-codex.description: Use the local Codex CLI as an independent second agent. Two branches — (1) proactively run `codex review` for a second opinion after completing a substantive change, before presenting it as done or committing; (2) delegate a well-defined implementation task via `codex exec`, ONLY when the user explicitly asks for Codex to do it. Also covers how to prompt Codex.

dzhng-skills-visual-compare-screenshots.description: Compare screenshots against the intended design, distinguishing approved references from historical baselines. Use for iterative implementation matching, before/after visual review, objective image telemetry, or checking a lone capture for flat, empty, or badly framed content.

dzhng-skills-visual-design-with-images.description: Explore UI and visual design with image generation, then iterate the real implementation against the user-selected concept. Use when brainstorming visual directions, offering mockup variants, or implementing an approved generated design; do not stop at the mockups or the first code approximation.

dzhng-skills-review-eli5.description: Explain a technical spec or proposed change in plain language: what problem it solves, how the solution works, and every schema change.

dzhng-skills-authoring-eval-skills.description: Eval and improve a skill against golden cases — run the target skill blind in a fresh, context-free subagent on each example input, grade the artifact against the expected outcome, and let the gaps drive the edits. Use when the user wants to test/eval/improve/harden a skill, says "this skill keeps producing X / keeps missing Y", or hands a skill plus example input→expected-output pairs. Pairs with [write-skills](../write-skills/SKILL.md) (the authoring principles every fix obeys).

dzhng-skills-plan-explore-unknowns.description: Guide the user through a quadrant walk that maps the unknowns of a task — open by listing the known knowns, then work through known unknowns, unknown knowns, and unknown unknowns one stage at a time, ending with a complete four-quadrant map in the user's hands. Use when a request is ambiguous or underspecified, the codebase or domain is unfamiliar, the user will "know it when they see it", a reference implementation must be understood before porting, mid-build deviations from the plan need capturing, or a finished change needs buy-in or verified understanding before merge. Pairs with…

dzhng-skills-review-find-overengineering.description: Find and roll back overengineering — protective code that solves an edge case of an edge case at the cost of far too much complexity, or careful migrations for a product with no users. Use when reviewing a diff or subsystem for unnecessary guards, fallbacks, validation, compatibility code or migrations, or when asked whether one is needed.

dzhng-skills-review-find-state-machines.description: Find implicit state machines, where one lifecycle's state, transitions, and ownership are scattered across flags, effects, callbacks, and async work, and make them explicit. Use when auditing lifecycle coordination, async flows, impossible states, or a proposed stateful refactor.

dzhng-skills-implement-handoff-spec.description: Hand a spec that is mid-implementation to another machine or another agent.

dzhng-skills-implement-implement-spec.description: Implement an existing spec through committed passes. Use for long or multi-pass specs that need maintenance checkpoints to periodically clean code, handoffs, priorities, and plan bloat before drift accumulates.

dzhng-skills-implement-implement-spec-wi.description: Run [implement-spec](../implement-spec/SKILL.md) with Codex doing the implementation passes while you orchestrate, integrate, and review. Use when the user asks to implement a spec with Codex, or to run implement-spec with Codex as the implementer.
Implement a spec using the harness's goal feature.

dzhng-skills-graphics-isometric-motion.description: Build animations and interactive elements (explainers, figures, hero visuals, step-through walkthroughs) in the crafted isometric "Anatomy" style, with many small precise solid parts, four-tone shading, correct painter's order, a framed card with title, hint and live readout, and calm eased motion. Works for physical machines and for abstract concepts (e.g. how an LLM picks its next token), as SVG/HTML or React/Next.js, with optional in-perspective WebGL shaders. Use this whenever someone wants an isometric animation, interactive element, explanatory diagram or figure for docs, a blog post, a…

dzhng-skills-graphics-launch-video.description: Make a showreel-grade motion-graphics launch video, with music, that introduces a CLI, library, or product from its repo. Use when asked for a launch, promo, sizzle, or showreel video, an animated intro for a project, or a video to post on X/social.

dzhng-skills-implement-marketing-pages.description: Best-practice rulebook for a marketing site's pages, organized by page class — campaign landers, product pages, programmatic SEO trees, editorial. Use when writing or updating a landing/marketing page, wiring a campaign lander to an attribution identifier, changing site-wide nav/footer links, touching sitemap/robots/agent-readable surfaces, or auditing a public site's indexing, reachability, and conversion setup.

dzhng-skills-implement-port-features.description: Port a feature from an existing repository by copying its actual code and editing the copy, so its bug fixes and behavioral nuances survive, then naturalizing it to this project's names and environment. Use when asked to copy or port an existing feature (especially an exact copy), when moving one into a different framework or host, or when a previous reimplementation missed upstream behavior.

dzhng-skills-visual-preview-shots.description: Open image shots (screenshots, snapshot baselines, montages, renders) in ONE macOS Preview window so the user can eyeball them. Use when the user asks to open / show / pull up / review shots in Preview or Finder, or right after producing visual artifacts the user should look at before signing off.

dzhng-skills-review-ratchet-files.description: Ratchet source file size so every file stays small enough for an agent to read whole: find every file over a token budget, split oversized files by concept, and set up the pre-commit ratchet that stops them from growing. Use when a commit is blocked because a file is over the size budget, when asked to find or split oversized/long/god files, when a file you need to change is too large to read in one pass, or when asked to add a file-size limit or hook to a repository or repair commit-hook coverage across worktrees.

dzhng-skills-review-refactor-change.description: Refactor cleanly instead of layering sediment. Use for rename requests, stale or misleading names, legacy leftovers, changed scope, or when a change reveals duplicated concepts, local adapters, obsolete owners, redundant inputs or guards, compatibility wrappers, parallel abstractions, an over-large module that has accreted many responsibilities, or "just tack this on" pressure in any code area.

dzhng-skills-review-refactor-codebase.description: Refactor a whole codebase in one run, tuned to clear the layered debt AI-written code piles up, so a typical change lands in one place. Worth running regularly.

dzhng-skills-graphics-renderer.description: Architecture rules for GPU rendering with TypeGPU/WebGPU. Use when adding or changing render passes, shaders, frame orchestration, GPU resources, culling, terrain, shadows, or visual performance work.

dzhng-skills-review-review.description: Closeout pass on a finished substantive change — sequence refactor-change (shape), code-review (diff), and write-docs (docs) so all three run, in the order where each feeds the next. Use after implementing a slice or feature and before calling it done or committing; when the user asks for a final review, a cleanup-and-document pass, or to "review everything." For a diff-only audit, reach code-review directly.

dzhng-skills-visual-screenshot-critique.description: Use the unprimed sub agent as a second set of eyes before accepting visual work — MANDATORY before declaring any user-reported visual bug fixed or claiming a visual change verified; primed eyes pass defects fresh eyes catch.

dzhng-skills-implement-write-docs.description: Write and edit project docs (README/markdown) as a glossary of principles, not a mirror of the code. Use when creating or revising a README; when a doc enumerates exact scenes, scenarios, helpers, class ids, file lists, or command/flag matrices the code already holds; when trimming narrative or changelog out of a doc; or when deduplicating overlapping docs and wiring a root doc to its sub-docs.

dzhng-skills-authoring-write-skills.description: Create or revise agent skills. Use when adding a new skill file, renaming a skill, simplifying an existing skill, improving trigger descriptions, or deciding what belongs in a skill versus references, scripts, assets, or ordinary docs.

dzhng-skills-plan-write-spec.description: Break large features into independently verifiable, human-reviewable slices under a feature directory in specs/. Use for risky or multi-step feature work that needs upfront questioning, API seams, browser-playable checkpoints, HTML visualizations, screenshot gates, staged implementation plans, recursive fog-of-war reslicing, or proactive research into reference implementations/best practices before slicing. Pairs with your project's verification harness and screenshot gates (the browser checkpoints), [refactor-change](../../review/refactor-change/SKILL.md) (review the materialized spec so the…

dzhng-skills-implement-write-tests.description: Write tests that pin real behavior instead of implementation details, config values, or lucky samples. Use when adding tests for new behavior, writing a regression test, fixing a brittle or flaky test, reviewing a test diff, or when a test breaks after a refactor or config change that didn't change behavior.

dzhng-skills-graphics-xiaohei-illustrati.description: Generate Ian-style Xiaohei illustrations for articles, posts, blogs, Notion documents, workflows, methods, processes, structures, states, metaphors, and opinions. Use when the user asks for weird, hand-drawn, Xiaohei, article, editorial, body illustrations, illustration ideas, shot lists, title removal, image edits, or image regeneration. By default, all image text and annotations are English, even when the source article is Chinese; only use another language when the user explicitly asks.
